from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Node:
    """A block or inline node; raw content is retained for later stages."""

    type: str
    children: list["Node"] = field(default_factory=list)
    raw: str = ""
    level: int | None = None
    literal: str = ""
    info: str = ""

    @property
    def raw_content(self) -> str:
        return self.raw


@dataclass
class Document:
    children: list[Node] = field(default_factory=list)
    references: dict[str, tuple[str, str | None]] = field(default_factory=dict)

def normalize_label(label: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r'[ \t\r\n]+', ' ', label.strip(' \t\r\n')).casefold()

    if pos >= len(text) or text[pos] not in '"\'(': return None
    op = text[pos]; cl = ')' if op == '(' else op; out=[]; i=pos+1
    while i < len(text):
        if text[i] == '\\' and i+1 < len(text):
            if text[i+1] not in "!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~": out.append('\\')
            out.append(text[i+1]); i += 2; continue
        if text[i] == cl: return ''.join(out), i+1
        if text[i] == '\n' and op == '(': return None
        out.append(text[i]); i += 1
    return None

    m = re.match(r'^ {0,3}\[', text)
    if not m: return None
    i=m.end(); label=[]

def collect_definitions(text: str, definitions: dict) -> str:
    # Definitions can be adjacent on separate lines. Parse a candidate from
    # each line boundary while preserving non-definition lines verbatim.

    # this function when closing the paragraph, so only definitions at its
    # beginning are eligible; subsequent lines remain paragraph text.
    kept = []
    i = 0
    paragraph_started = False
    while i < len(lines):
        if paragraph_started:
            kept.extend(lines[i:])
            break
        parsed = _definition(''.join(lines[i:]))
        if parsed:
            label, destination, title, end = parsed
            if label not in definitions:
                definitions[label] = (destination, title)
            consumed = ''.join(lines[i:])[:end].count('\n')
            i += max(1, consumed)
        else:
            kept.append(lines[i]); i += 1
            if lines[i-1].strip():
                paragraph_started = True
    return ''.join(kept)

item.text: The failures cluster into three causes: reference definitions are consumed with incorrect line boundaries (including titles and multiline labels), angle destinations mishandle escaped or invalid delimiters, and inline parsing lacks image-aware bracket precedence. I’m fixing those shared paths and will check the scoped examples afterward.
